A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UCB-V asymptotics and regret study. Their text, equations, four figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: Figures 1–4 report original repeated bandit simulations measuring arm-pulling counts, regret, and empirical Z-statistic distributions.

after.justification: Figures 1–4 retain original simulation results on arm allocation, regret, and inference under UCB and UCB-V.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same initialization, empirical estimates, confidence bonus, and arm-selection rule. The discussion of modifications to historical UCB-V moves from Appendix F to Appendix G without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: The same synthetic two-arm bandit scenarios and variance/gap regimes are evaluated. The new Gaussian and bounded-distribution constructions in Appendix H support theoretical proofs, not additional experiments.

E2.justification: Canonical UCB remains the algorithmic comparator in the corresponding simulations. No additional method is experimentally evaluated; other algorithms remain literature comparisons.

E3.justification: The stated simulation horizons, variance/gap settings, and measurements of regret, arm counts, and Z-statistics remain unchanged. Redrawn axes and histogram labels do not establish a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The same variance-sensitivity experiments, perturbation-stability analysis, and stable/unstable inference case studies remain in Figures 2–4. No additional ablation or robustness question is evaluated.

E5.justification: Empirical shaded variability bands visible in v1 Figures 2a, 2b, and 3a disappear in v2. Repetition counts and captions referring to 30% quantiles remain unchanged; the theoretical bound curves are retained.

E6.justification: Figure 2a changes reported regret values under the same stated setting: at T = 50,000, the sigma_1 approximately T^(-1/4) curve changes from roughly 58 to 55. The advantage of the high-variance optimal arm remains. The PDFs do not identify whether the update reflects rerunning or correcting the plot.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 8 with worst-case and conditional trade-off regret lower bounds. New Appendix H supplies Gaussian constructions through Theorem 23 and bounded-distribution constructions and KL bounds through Lemma 24. Existing stability and regret upper-bound results are largely retained.

C1.justification: V1 ends Section 5 by conjecturing optimality and leaving lower bounds to future work. V2 adds a central two-arm optimality claim in Section 4 based on matching lower bounds under stated instance and policy restrictions. The broader K-arm conjecture paragraph is removed.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly interprets the lower bounds separately for the two optimal-versus-suboptimal variance regimes, including the restriction to policies with good worst-case performance. Existing explanations of instability, inference failure, and incomplete K-arm stability characterization remain.

D1.justification: Existing pseudocode, simulation parameter disclosures, and details of the modified UCB-V bonus are retained. No new implementation instructions, hardware information, or code/data access information appears.

R1.justification: The bibliography is unchanged. However, Appendix A corrects the comparison with Zhang et al. (2021) and Zhao et al. (2023), explicitly restricting agreement to homogeneous variance settings and stating that general-case guarantees are not directly comparable.

P1.justification: V2 edits prose throughout and substantially reorganizes the exposition: related work becomes Appendix A, notation and organization become run-in paragraphs, the earlier regret derivation is condensed into a footnote, and literature comparisons move to Section 5. References move before the appendices; the title and author block also change.

P2.justification: All four figures are redrawn with different styling, colors, legends, axis labels, and ranges. Figure 4 removes histogram bars and displays density curves; Figures 2–3 remove empirical shading. Figure placement relative to the surrounding text also changes.

improvement.justification: V2 adds potentially important optimality analysis absent from v1 and clarifies comparison assumptions. However, Theorem 8's equation (13) states a sqrt(T/c_T) factor, while Appendix H's argument in equations (53) and (56) targets sqrt(T)/c_T, leaving the stated dependence unresolved. Together with removed empirical variability bands, this prevents a confident net quality judgment.
